messages:
nate: Heads-up — NimbusPay on Dedicated (ded-142) is hitting ~15s tail latencies and a bunch of 429s starting ~09:12 UTC. They also report intermittent 401s and unexpected extra hosted charges. Customer sent logs, attaching link: <https://s3.redwood.internal/nimbuspay/escalation.log>

maria: taking this. Can you drop a brief summary (error snippets + top metrics) so I can triage + loop eng? :eyes:

nate: Summary:
- 429s spike correlates with kvcache eviction bursts, kvcache_util ~94% and eviction rate ~820/min at spike.
- sample log lines:```
[09:12:23] kvcache: evict prefix="conv:acct:987" ctx_len=12288 size=17.3KB
[09:12:23] memfrag: slab_realloc: failed to find contiguous slab (wanted 64MB)
[09:12:24] router: fallback to hosted-embed-v2 for tenant=987 cause="dedicated_throttle"
[09:12:25] auth: token validate failed tenant=987 err=\"token revoked\" status=401
```
- autoscaler did not add nodes during spike; desired_replicas stayed at 6. There are short-lived noisy workloads from tenant 987 long-context requests (avg ctx_len ~11k).
- Billing: fallback requests go to hosted model, customer sees unexpected hosted token usage.

maria: pinging @sam and @lee from eng-sre/infra to help reproduce and propose mitigations.

sam: thanks. first pass — sounds like kvcache fragmentation + large long-context tails causing repeated evictions and heavy GC cycles. That can block autoscaler because pods are staying up but starved, so scale doesn't help.

sam: Can you share a minimal repro? nate: if you can get a curl that reproduces the long context flood that would help.

nate: repro we use in support:```bash
TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "x-dedicated-id: ded-142" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-serve-v1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"keep this convo very long"},{"role":"user","content":"'$(python -c 'print("A"*12000)')'"}] }'
```
This produces the eviction wave within ~3-5 concurrent clients.

lee: repro looks good. A few quick checks:
- confirm kvcache slab sizes: `rtdctl get-config ded-142 --field kvcache.slab_sizes`
- check node-level fragmentation: `node-exporter /proc/meminfo` and `pmap` on worst pods
- autoscaler logs: `kubectl -n infra logs deployment/autoscaler` (look for reasons why it kept desired_replicas)

sam: immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Add temporary tenant QoS to throttle tenant 987 at edge (rate-limit long-contexts) — support can request this.
2) Set routing policy for ded-142 to avoid immediate fallback to hosted: `api->routing set ded-142 --fallback=fail` (prevents extra hosted billing).
3) Increase kvcache slab target on ded-142: `rtdctl set-config ded-142 --kvcache-slab-gb=48` (weird fragmentation may need 48-96GB to reduce realloc churn).
4) Roll a small patch to allocator to prefer smaller slabs until compaction finishes (eng-infra follow-up).

maria: can support enact 1 + 2 now? I can notify NimbusPay about temporary QoS. Also need to confirm billing rollback for hosted charges.

nate: I can apply QoS throttle for tenant 987 now (rate-limit long prompts to 5/min). Applying... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: [09:15:02] autoscaler: evaluate cluster=ded-us-3 desired=6 current=6 reason=scale_blocked reason_detail="alloc_util stable but kvcache_fragmentation>0.80"

alex: quick security note — please scrub tokens from any pasted logs before sharing externally. We saw a token in the S3 log bundle; rotated it already for ded-142.

sam: next steps for eng:
- infra: run compaction job on nodes hosting ded-142 to defragment memory slabs (low-risk rolling restart).
- runtime: instrument kvcache to emit contiguous slab free list metrics and add alert at 0.85.
- autoscaler: change decision to consider kvcache_fragmentation and not just cpu/mem.
- product: add tenant-level fallback billing flag so hosted fallback charges can be suppressed while under incident.

maria: owners and ETA?

sam: infra (lee) — compaction rolling restart in 30m, estimate 20m window. runtime (sam) — small instrument + alert by EOD. autoscaler change is larger, will triage and aim for next week. product (maria) — will scope billing rollback with finance, need ticket.

lee: started compaction job on nodes n-ded-03a/n-ded-03b. Watching memory and eviction rate. So far eviction_rate down 60% after first node compaction.

customer-bot: NimbusPay: thanks for the quick response. Please keep us updated on expected restored throughput; 401s are causing payment flow failures.

maria: I will send a status update to NimbusPay: we applied tenant QoS to stop long-context floods, prevented fallback billing by disabling fallback, and are doing rolling compaction on nodes. Expect follow-up after compaction completes.

sam: tagging this as P2 incident -> create incident/DED-KVCACHE-334567 for tracking and postmortem.

maria: closing loop here — will paste postmortem link when ready. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
